hypotheses.justification: `hV` is used only to build `hF : ∀ X ∈ {V,W}, IsCode c X`, which is needed only by `supCode_le_iff` in the direction `supCode c {V,W} ⊆ U`. That direction can be proved without knowing V is a code: `supCode c {V,W} = regular c (sUnion {V,W})`, so by `mem_regular` (InternalRegularAlgebra.lean, line 11: `p ∈ regular c U ↔ p ∈ c ∧ ∀ q ∈ c, p ⊆ q → ∃ r ∈ U, q ⊆ r`) an element `p` of `supCode c {V,W}` lies in `c` and satisfies: for every `q ∈ c` with `p ⊆ q` there is `r ∈ sUnion {V,W}` with `q ⊆ r`. Any such `r` lies in `V` or `W`, hence in `U` by `h.1` / `h.2.1`; so `mem_regular` gives `p ∈ regular c U = U` (using `hU.2`). The reverse inclusion `U ⊆ supCode c {V,W}` is the original argument and uses only `hU` (`code_lower`) and `h`. Note this proof also removes the need for `hW`, so both `hV` and `hW` can be deleted simultaneously.

Same as for `hV`: `hW` only feeds the `hF` argument of `supCode_le_iff`. The inclusion `supCode c {V,W} ⊆ U` follows directly from `mem_regular` plus `W ⊆ U` (`h.2.1`), without W being a code; the other inclusion uses only `hU`, `code_lower`, `mem_regular` and the Partition clause. Hence the statement remains true and provable with `hW` deleted (and likewise with `hV` deleted at the same time).
